patches.reason: A refused RabbitMQ connection ended the harness (review finding R2, PC-NUQ-CONNECT).
After a broker restart the listener was never re-established while the process survived (review finding R1, upstream #4244 / PR #4263).
The engine registration and result translation spec §8.1 requires; every page acquisition goes to the retrieval service.
File downloads and map's redirect resolution fetched directly with the core's own dispatcher (spec §8.4).
Search fell back to DuckDuckGo over the home connection whenever SearXNG was unset or empty (evidence/M0/source-review.json S15).
The upstream Dockerfile floats every base image, the Rust toolchain and the crate graph, and downloads the FoundationDB client unchecked (decisions D4, D6).

A search backend failure became an empty result at three layers: searxng_search and search both returned {} on any error, and patch 0005 returned {} when SearXNG had no results (review finding S6, spec §13).

Native PDF parsing returned empty markdown as success for a scan-only document, had no page cap, and fell back to a pdf-parse whose bundled pdf.js 1.10 refuses some valid files; spec §15 asks for native parsing first, typed refusals and a budgeted complex-document fallback.

The scrape option proxy (auto, basic, stealth) never reached the retrieval service, so a caller could not ask for the residential route and a bulk job's pages could not start on it (spec §10.2); proxyUsed always said basic.

The enhanced proxy option was refused and screenshots and actions were unregistered, so M7 could offer neither (spec §11, §12); an engine result with target status 401, 403 or 429 would start upstream's AddFeatureError retry outside the page's budget; and the parse cache's owner was the core's single team id (M5 review S1).
